parallel.requirements: Recognized the C++ test1 port requirements: pure Rust, std only, Cargo project, package-root test1.rs, argument acceptance, byte-identical output, and black-box inference from the reference binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept implementation ownership, produced the Rust project, then launched a large verifier workflow for adversarial audits while continuing local work.
parallel.implementation: Created Cargo.toml, test1.rs, modular point/path/rect library code, README, and compiled artifacts; patched edition compatibility, stdout error handling, non-UTF-8 argv, and overflow behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all final source changes in the parent-owned /output tree; child agents did not deliver implementation components to merge.
parallel.verification: Ran cargo build/test, standalone rustc across editions, differential output matrices, byte-level argument checks, and then passed the official evaluator 62/62.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The verifier workflow was interrupted and the final response was empty, but current artifact validation and official evaluation show no accepted-deliverable shortfall.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure Rust, Cargo, std-only, root test1.rs, and reference-output obligations from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned implementation, integration, build, testing, and final response without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: Created a compact Cargo project with core/path modules under src/clipper2, root test1.rs, Cargo.lock, and compiled test1 executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Wrote and delivered a coherent project tree directly, including the expected executable and Cargo release artifact.
serial.verification: Ran cargo build --release, cargo test --release, standalone rustc, differential cases against the C++ reference, and byte-level stdout comparison.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task-relevant work is visible at closure; final response notes completion, verification, and minor caveats.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent identified pure Rust, no external crates, Cargo layout, root test1.rs, argument compatibility, and byte-identical output, then adjusted implementation details to satisfy those requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent identified the same prompt obligations and created a Cargo project with test1.rs, library modules, and matching output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap caused an outcome difference; the parallel run spent more effort hardening edge cases, while serial implemented a simpler accepted slice.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and later spawned a verifier workflow of many read-only auditors and refuters after an initial candidate existed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no subagents and kept all implementation, build, and verification work in one local trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition added audit concurrency but did not delegate required implementation ownership; serial was linear and simpler.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow children received a detailed audit brief about the current /output port and returned verifier findings, some of which became stale as the parent patched the shared artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not transfer context across agent boundaries; all observed task knowledge remained in the same actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel workflow produced stale or conflicting audit findings during active parent edits, but the parent resolved the material ones locally before official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built a broader module set with point, path, rect, README, root binary, and multiple post-audit patches for edition, IO, argv, and overflow behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a compact clipper2 module tree with core/path modules and a root test1.rs that prints the Path64 size.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented accepted Rust ports; parallel carried extra generalized API work and edge hardening, serial carried a smaller implementation surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The verifier workflow returned partial findings and refutations, but the aggregate workflow was still in progress when the parent process was interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run completed local verification and then produced a normal final response summarizing the delivered files and checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had incomplete audit-result lifecycle and empty final response, but not an incomplete deliverable; serial had clean closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the parent edited /output; child agents audited and reported while the parent patched files, so no child-owned implementation was overwritten or merged.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote its project files directly without concurrent workspace actors or merge points.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared a live artifact with auditors, creating stale observations but no concrete write collision or provenance-breaking overwrite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran Cargo tests, standalone rustc checks, edition checks, and broad differential matrices including non-UTF-8 argument comparisons before official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran Cargo build/test, standalone rustc, differential comparisons, and byte-level stdout comparison before official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified enough to pass the official evaluator; parallel verification was broader and partially workflow-assisted, serial verification was local and sufficient.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed nearly the full cell budget, returned code 143, and had no final response text, but artifact validation and official evaluation succeeded.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 348.72 seconds with return code 0 and a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was budget-stressed because of the large audit workflow; serial closure was normal, yet the accepted artifact result was the same.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 62 of 62 tests, so there is no discordant outcome. Parallel differed by using a large verifier workflow after parent-led implementation and by timing out with an empty final response, while serial completed a smaller direct implementation and final message. The accepted artifact result did not differ.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation plus broad audit workflow produced a passing artifact despite workflow interruption.
serial_contributors: Single-agent implementation and local verification produced a passing artifact with normal closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel produced a broader library/README and more edge-case hardening; serial produced a smaller accepted project.
Parallel final response was empty after process interruption; serial final response was complete.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process contrast only

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly owned and performed implementation before and after the workflow; children were auditors, so implementation was not ownerless.
There were no separately owned implementation components needing reconciliation; the parent integrated all source edits itself.
The parent created the Cargo project, root test1.rs, compiled binaries, README, and deliverable tree; assembly was owned.
The parent drove implementation, build, local differential checks, and final artifact production, so the end-to-end pipeline had an owner despite timeout.
Implementation was not blocked behind a serial preflight; the parent implemented a candidate before launching the audit workflow.
The workflow was an audit phase after productive implementation began, not an investigation phase that deferred implementation and caused unfinished delivery.
Although many auditors ran, the indispensable implementation path stayed with the parent and reached an accepted artifact.
The broad verifier workflow contributed to timeout, but no required implementation, integration, or evaluator-aligned verification was displaced from the accepted artifact.
No single child owned an indispensable overbroad implementation scope; children audited/refuted findings and unfinished child work was not needed for acceptance.
Child briefs were audit briefs over the current port; no known requirement omitted from a child brief produced unusable work or an unmet required stage.
Children did not independently implement components expected to interoperate, so no missing cross-agent source or API contract produced incompatibility.
No known requirement or finding disappeared across transfer; parent-visible issues such as non-UTF-8 args were eventually acted on.
Returned audit material was large and mixed, but the parent used relevant findings and still completed accepted implementation and verification.
Some child findings described superseded files during parent edits, but stale reports did not cause a wrong final integration or failed evaluation.
Verifier/refuter disagreement was inspected in the workflow journal and did not remain an unadjudicated integration blocker.
The parent did not merely accept a workflow result; it ran local builds and differential checks, and the official evaluation later passed.
The workflow included refuters, but there is no replacement attempt that repeated prior work without inherited findings and caused budget loss or failure.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The run interrupted active workflow children, but their audit work was not required to finalize the already accepted deliverable, so the adverse consequence gate is not met.
A complete deliverable was already present and passed artifact validation/evaluation; no promotable candidate was left unplaced before closure.
The parent rebuilt and retested after later source changes such as args_os; there is no child result merged after final verification without a post-merge check.
No child produced a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or merge; children were verifiers rather than implementers.
Some verifier work was interrupted, but concrete findings did return through the journal and unresolved aggregate return was not needed for accepted delivery.
Interrupted or refuted verifier children did not own required task scope, and the parent took over material fixes before closure.
The parent inspected workflow progress and acted on material audit findings; available completed results were not simply ignored with a contrary final state.
The parent waited for workflow progress at times but also inspected status and continued local fixes/tests, so this was not an uninspected wait that displaced necessary work.
Only the parent wrote implementation files; auditor children read and reported, so no competing cross-file implementation designs required reconciliation.
No live child edited the same source file as the parent, so there was no same-file race to reconcile.
There is no evidence that one actor replaced source owned or produced by another actor; parent edits were sequential within its own ownership.
The parent rebuilt executables, but no concurrent child owned or consumed the deliverable being overwritten.
No cleanup or broad promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Although auditors shared visibility into /output, they were read-only under the workflow brief; shared workspace visibility did not cause unstable writes.
No child-generated artifact, cache, fixture, or auxiliary tool was consumed as stable implementation input or reference evidence by the parent.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Workflow timeout, incomplete child returns, stale verifier findings, and empty final response were treated as one reviewed chain; none met the realized adverse task-consequence gate for a retained label.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were reviewed; near misses around timeout, fan-out, stale handoffs, unused results, and shared workspace were rejected because the delivered artifact passed and no required child-owned work was lost.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained merely for child count, elapsed time, timeout, stale audit observations, or parallel usage; no target distribution or numeric cap was applied.
